topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement's importance and warning about its complicated nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the complement cascade is organized and understood, culminating in C3 cleavage as its central activating event.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition produces enough surface-bound C3b to cross the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement brings about pathogen clearance.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how complement regulators restrain activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of individual complement components to the clinical consequences of their deficiency.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains pathogen adaptations that impede complement, extending the protein A example to applications of its antibody-binding activity.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture series and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
